summary_paragraph: A woman with sickle cell disease, osteosarcoma, and chronic hepatitis C was admitted with odynophagia, fever, and hypotension five days after missing her Neupogen injection. She presented with septic shock and profound neutropenia, requiring ICU admission, vasopressor support, broad-spectrum antibiotics, antifungal therapy, and blood transfusions. Her condition stabilized with treatment, and she improved clinically and laboratory-wise over five days. White blood cell count recovered with Neupogen, hemoglobin improved post-transfusion, and platelets remained low at discharge. Her odynophagia was managed symptomatically and resolved. She was discharged home with instructions to avoid NSAIDs, monitor for bleeding, obtain outpatient lab testing, and follow up with her oncology and primary care teams for ongoing management of thrombocytopenia, GERD, and thyroid abnormalities.
